verdict: Ventas grew revenue 23% to $1.83B as its senior-housing operating portfolio surged, and it raised full-year guidance after closing $5.2B of senior-housing investments so far this year.

kpis.label: Normalized FFO per share
kpis.note: +10% YoY — the cash measure REIT investors watch

segments.name: Resident fees & services
segments.note: Rent and care fees from senior-housing communities Ventas operates itself (the SHOP portfolio) — now by far the biggest revenue line, boosted by acquisitions.

segments.name: Rental income
segments.note: Rent from properties leased to tenants: outpatient medical and research buildings ($233M) and triple-net leased properties ($129M), where the tenant pays most property costs.

segments.name: Income from loans & investments
segments.note: Income from loans and other investments.

segments.name: Third-party fees & other
segments.note: Third-party capital management revenues ($4M) plus interest and other income ($2M).

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of the buildings over their lives — a large non-cash charge that FFO adds back.

opex.name: G&A & professional fees
opex.note: Running the company and professional fees.

opex.name: Transaction & restructuring
opex.note: Transaction, transition and restructuring costs, mostly deal-related.

opex.name: Third-party capital mgmt
opex.note: Costs of managing capital for third parties.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $161M and a $5M loss from unconsolidated entities, partly offset by a $1M gain on real estate dispositions.

takeaways.title: Senior housing is powering growth
takeaways.text: Total company net operating income rose 18% YoY, led by the senior-housing operating portfolio, where same-store cash NOI grew 16% — 17% in the U.S.

takeaways.title: Buying into the demographic wave
takeaways.text: Ventas has closed $5.2B of senior-housing investments so far in 2026 and raised full-year guidance again, betting on the wave of Baby Boomers turning 80.

takeaways.title: Cash earnings vs accounting profit
takeaways.text: GAAP net income was just $67M after $446M of depreciation and $161M of interest — but Normalized FFO, the cash-style measure, was $514M, or $0.99 per share, up 10%.

footerNote: Direct costs are property-level operating expenses ($1,105M), mostly the cost of staffing and running the senior-housing communities. Interest expense sits below operating profit, following the REIT pattern used on this site. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $65M; the tax line is a $19M benefit.
